THE RULES OF THIS BOARD — permanent, they never come off

  1. Your list goes up here first. Every item you raise becomes a card with a BEFORE picture, an AFTER picture and how I would fix it. Nothing is written into the planner before that.
  2. No code before you approve the card. You approve card by card. Only when you say “make it live” do I write anything.
  3. Approved is not live. A card you approve stays here as APPROVED until the build ships, so you can see what is queued.
  4. A card never leaves until you say remove. This board is the record of what you asked for, not a list of what I finished.
  5. Your words are kept, all of them — one line per thing you said. Your first quote stays at the top of the card forever; every later correction is its own dated line underneath, never merged into a paragraph, so you can check each one off. I never replace what you said with my summary.
  6. The AFTER is not one picture — it explains the new setup, step by step, in different pictures. What happens first, what happens next, what it looks like when it works. Never the same picture twice. If nothing is built yet, the card says so in plain words instead of pretending.
  7. Every question sits inside the problem it belongs to — never collected somewhere else. You read one card and answer it there.
  8. I raise what you have not thought of. Every card carries an I also thought of note: the thing your request does not decide — the crowded case, the phone, what happens to what you already have.
  9. I test it in Safari myself — before I call it done, and again after it goes live.
  10. Pictures, not paragraphs. Short words around the picture, never an essay above it.
  11. Every picture is half a page — including the step pictures. The BEFORE and AFTER are half each, and a step picture is the same size, not a thumbnail, because you have to see what is inside it. A shot of the whole browser takes the full width on its own row.
  12. EVERY APPROVED CARD IS SHOWN CONSOLIDATED — folded shut. The moment you approve one it collapses to a single line, so the board only ever shows you what still needs you. Press open beside its number to look at it again. This one is never skipped.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

You found this and asked how I missed it. Here is the honest answer.

What you see: you press + on Reminder, pick a day, press Set — and nothing appears. The row still shows only the +. So the feature looks dead.

What is actually happening: the alarm IS being kept — but in the dialog’s own list, which is not written onto the task until you press Save. The chip on screen reads the task. So between Set and Save there is genuinely nothing to show.

How I missed it: I checked that the reminder was stored — it went from 0 to 1 — and called that working. I never looked at the screen. The data was right and the feature was broken, and my check could not tell the difference.

How I fix it: while the dialog is open, the chip reads the list the dialog is holding — the same list Save will write. Press Set and the chip is there at once.

So it cannot happen again: every check from now on asserts what is on the screen, never only what is stored.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

You asked how I would set it up, so here it is in full.

1. When the reminder is due it appears as it does now.
2. If you do nothing, it comes back at 5 minutes, then 15, then 30 — widening, so it nags less as time goes on rather than more.
3. Each repeat looks different from the first. It carries a count — “2nd reminder · due 25 min ago” — so you can tell at a glance this is not a fresh one.
4. It stops after one hour and leaves a quiet marker on the item, so nothing nags you forever but nothing vanishes silently either.
5. Acknowledging means pressing Got it (stops it) or Snooze (restarts the ladder). Opening the task also counts — if you acted on it, you acknowledged it.
6. Coming back after being away: ONE catch-up line, “tried 4 times”, never four stacked pop-ups.

The honest limit: this only fires while a planner tab is open. A true phone alarm that fires with the planner closed is a different mechanism and I would have to price it separately — say if you want that and I will put it up as its own card.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

What it was. Every row printed the raw stored value — 2026-09-26 01:44 — year first, 24-hour clock: the shape the data is saved in rather than the shape you read in.

What it is now. 9/26/26 1:44 AM. Month, day, two-digit year, then a 12-hour time. The font and the alignment are untouched, as you said.

Your rule about February — already satisfied, and I checked it rather than assuming. You asked that a single-digit month read 2 and not 02. The month is built from a number, so it never pads: 2/5/26 9:05 AM. The hour behaves the same way — 1:44 AM, not 01:44. The only zero that survives is in the MINUTES (9:05, never 9:5), because a minute is positional — without it, five past nine and fifty past nine would both read 9:5. Tell me if you want that one dropped too.

I did not write a new date formatter. The planner already had one short-date style; it now feeds this list, so the alarms read the same way as every other terse date in the app and there is a single place to change it.

All three tabs, pressed rather than assumed.
